The BMW M6 Convertible Now Costs Virtually Nothing in the States
14 photos
Photo: Cars&Bids
Mind you, this is still a great open-top grand tourer with a focus on performance, which has aged like fine wine, packs plenty of features, and has a great V8 engine under the hood.
The last generation preceded the M8, and was offered in three body styles, just like its successor, These included the F13 Coupe, the F12 Convertible, and the F06 Gran Coupe, all of which had a front-engine and rear-wheel drive layout, and used the same 4.4-liter V8 engine with twin turbos, mated to a six-speed manual transmission or a seven-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission.
The 2012 BMW M6 Convertible pictured in the gallery had 553 horsepower (560 ps/412 kW) to play with and 502 pound-feet (680 Nm) of torque, and everything is channeled to the (rear) wheels through a dual-clutch seven-speed automatic transmission. From 0 to 60 mph (0 to 97 kph), it needed just 4.3 seconds officially, and its top speed was 155 mph (250 kph). The latter number increased to 190 mph (305 kph) on cars equipped with the optional M Driver’s Pack.
According to the spec sheet, this machine features the Driver Assistance Package and the Executive Package. It rides on 20-inch wheels (343M), has a power-retractable ragtop, full Merino leather upholstery, a heated steering wheel, and carbon fiber trim. There are no notable modifications mentioned in the ad, and there is nothing to be worried about when it comes to the known issues.
Photo: Cars&Bids That’s because this BMW M6 Convertible has scratches on the wheels, a cracked door mirror casing on the right side, wear on the headlight lenses, chips and scratches on the outside, some of which have been touched up, and some wear on the seats and interior surfaces. The dealer reported that the rear bumper has been repainted, and there is a mileage inconsistency in September 2016, though the vendor noted it “a clerical error,” the ad shows.
At the time of cataloging, this open-top, V8-powered grand tourer had 60,700 miles (97,700 km) on the clock. The car features a San Marino Blue Metallic paint finish, a black cockpit, and has a clean Texas title, being located in Lewisville, TX, prior to the sale that we will get to in a few moments.
It had it engine oil and filter changed, the brake fluid flushed, and the cabin air filter replaced / cleaned at 55,864 miles (89,953 km), in April of 2023, and in March 2022, this ride had its four tires replaced, an alignment performed, the engine oil and filter changed, and the cabin air filter replaced / cleaned, at 52,655 miles (84,740 km).
The vendor, a used car dealer, reportedly bought this BMW M6 Convertible in September 2026, adding some 150 miles (240 km) since, and since they are in this game to make money, the listed it for grabs on Cars&Bids. The online auction ended on October 9, 2026, and when the gavel hit the table, this machine ended up changing hands for $19,250. That’s basically nothing considered that this thing had an MSRP of roughly $114,000 back in the day.
Photo: Cars&Bids But was it a steal, or is this pretty much the usual selling price for the 2012 model year BMW M6 Convertible? The answer leans on the latter, because on average, this model now fetched between $16,000 and close to $30,000. The latter sum is obviously reserved for nicely-maintained examples that have not seen that much action over the years. Used car dealers usually sell it between $24,000 and $28,000, and the high-mileage units that are not exactly top notch fetch less than $20,000 in today’s used car market.
Nevertheless, paying less than $20K for what is still a great driver’s car and an awesome daily that features a V8 engine paired with a smooth-shifting automatic transmission that delivers everything to the rear axle is something to write home about in our book, because this remains a fantastic ride if properly maintained. And speaking of that, it’s not exactly reliable, as there are plenty of things that can go wrong, especially with the powertrain, and some electrical goodies.
Therefore, one should be ready to cough out a lot of money on the maintenance, and this is pretty much the reason for the often low selling price of these things. Nevertheless, the FX-generation of the BMW M6 remains a lot of car for the money, and let’s be honest, it has aged like fine wine, hasn’t it? This applies to all body styles, but to me, the two-door coupe looks absolutely perfect, and so does the four-door sedan, and I have to admit that I’m not necessarily a fan of the convertible variant.
If you want to check out the pictured 2012 BMW M6 Convertible in more detail, then you can do so here , though don’t forget to tell us if you would have paid almost $20K on this example before you click that link.
